headline: Minesweeper's flags learned to shield the chord
lede: The never-dry rung named Minesweeper as the shelf's weakest title and it earned the score: a satisfied chord could detonate a correctly flagged mine — the impossible-looking `end=dead 71/71` QA pinned from CI. The fix is one line of fidelity: the original's chord clicks covered unflagged cells only, and now the engine finally agrees with its own solver.

notes.text: Chord shielding shipped (#3009/#3010, main ef15bf6): correct flags are never fatal, wrong flags still kill the original's way — by satisfying the clue while the real mine stays unflagged. sweepplay went 38/40 → 40/40; the death was reproducible 2/10 before and 0/12 after.
sweepcheck gained a fifth anchored mutant, flag-devour, plus a chord probe — the dig-only battery was structurally blind to chord bugs, so this class of regression can no longer slip green.
#3008's suggested post-win assertion is now pinned in the static gate: a fully swept board is WON the instant the safe total is hit, and every verb is refused after it.

When the engine and the solver disagree about a rule, one of them is lying about the original — diff the two rule tables before you touch a threshold. The solver had the shield right for a hundred checks while the engine ate its flags.
